Identified Flaws & Areas for Improvement ### 🔴 Critical / High-Impact #### 1. Massive GestureState Copying — O(n) Field-by-Field Copy Every Call [gesture.py:333-372](file:///Users/jerold/dev/Bricks/shared/gesture.py#L333-L372) `get_state()` manually copies **35+ fields** one-by-one into a new `GestureState`. This is fragile (add a field to the dataclass, forget to copy it here → silent bug) and already happened — any new field requires updates in two places. > [!WARNING] > **Fix**: Use `dataclasses.replace(self.state)` or `copy.copy(self.state)` under the lock. Or, since `GestureState` is a frozen snapshot, make it `@dataclass(frozen=True)` and assign atomically. #### 2. Game Launch Code is Copy-Pasted in main.py [main.py:292-321](file:///Users/jerold/dev/Bricks/main.py#L292-L321) Each game branch repeats: `game = XGame(cur, clock, debug=debug, mode=mode, audio=audio, username=username)` → `game.run(gesture_src)` → `debug = game._debug`. Five identical blocks that differ only in the class name. > [!TIP] > **Fix**: Create a `GAME_REGISTRY` dict mapping name → class, then `game = GAME_REGISTRY[selected](...)`. #### 3. No Base Game Class — Massive Code Duplication Across Games Each game file (bricks: 876, snake: 730, fruit_ninja: 1300, calibration: 1000) independently re-implements: - `_init_layout()` with identical scale/font logic - `_toggle_fullscreen()` - Learn/test submode switching (`_switch_submode`, `_init_learner`) - Debug overlay rendering - Pause/resume screen - Keyboard event handling boilerplate > [!IMPORTANT] > **Fix**: Extract a `BaseGame` class with common layout, fullscreen toggling, learn/test infrastructure, debug HUD, and a `_tick(dt, gs)` method games override. #### 4. `_emit_sample()` Called Twice per IMU Frame in Raw Mode [sensor.py:796-806](file:///Users/jerold/dev/Bricks/shared/sensor.py#L792-L806) `_parse_acc` calls `_emit_sample()`, then `_parse_gyro` also calls `_emit_sample()`. In raw mode, acc and gyro arrive as separate notifications, so the queue gets **two samples per physical frame** — one with stale gyro, one with stale acc. This doubles the effective processing rate and introduces a one-notification-lag cross-contamination. > [!CAUTION] > **Fix**: Only emit when both acc and gyro have been updated since the last emission (use a dirty-flag pair). #### 5. `sys.exit(0)` Called from Multiple Locations [home.py:206-207](file:///Users/jerold/dev/Bricks/home.py#L206-L207), [home.py:245-246](file:///Users/jerold/dev/Bricks/home.py#L245-L246), [magic_wand/game.py:124](file:///Users/jerold/dev/Bricks/games/magic_wand/game.py#L123-L124) `pygame.quit(); sys.exit(0)` bypasses the `finally` block in `main.py`, which means `gesture_src.stop()` and `sensor.stop_background()` never run. BLE connection is leaked, sensor LED stays on. > [!CAUTION] > **Fix**: Return a sentinel like `"quit"` from `run()` and let `main.py` handle shutdown. --- ### 🟡 Medium-Impact #### 6. Excessive Console Logging in Production `sensor.py` prints every 50th sample, every SF notification, first 20 notifications, etc. `gesture.py` prints every 10th sample. In a 10-minute play session, that's ~6,000+ print calls. **Fix**: Gate behind `logger.debug()` instead of `print()`, so `--verbose` controls visibility. #### 7. Magic Numbers Scattered Throughout - `45.0` (gyro threshold for baseline adaptation) in [gesture.py:436](file:///Users/jerold/dev/Bricks/shared/gesture.py#L436) - `0.002` (adapt rate) in [gesture.py:439](file:///Users/jerold/dev/Bricks/shared/gesture.py#L439) - `2.5 * 100` (functional cal duration) in [gesture.py:454](file:///Users/jerold/dev/Bricks/shared/gesture.py#L454) - `200.0` in spin scaling: [gesture.py:546](file:///Users/jerold/dev/Bricks/shared/gesture.py#L546) **Fix**: Move to `GestureConfig` fields. #### 8. `PowerUp.draw()` Creates a New Font Every Frame [bricks/game.py:162](file:///Users/jerold/dev/Bricks/games/bricks/game.py#L161-L163) `pygame.font.SysFont("monospace", font_size, bold=True)` is called inside `draw()` which runs 60 times/sec. Font creation is expensive. **Fix**: Cache the font at init time or use the game's existing font instances. #### 9. No Error Recovery for BLE Disconnection Mid-Game If the sensor disconnects during gameplay (battery dies, range exceeded), the gesture queue simply stops producing samples. The `_loop` in `gesture.py` keeps trying `queue.get(timeout=0.05)` and decays velocity, but there's no user feedback, no reconnection attempt, and no fallback to keyboard. **Fix**: Detect prolonged empty queue → show "sensor disconnected" overlay → offer keyboard fallback. #### 10. `_update_hover()` Sets `_selected_idx` as Side Effect [home.py:262](file:///Users/jerold/dev/Bricks/home.py#L253-L263) Mouse hover silently changes the keyboard/gesture selection index. This means if you're navigating with tilt and accidentally move the mouse, the selection jumps unexpectedly. **Fix**: Separate mouse highlight from the authoritative `_selected_idx`. #### 11. No High-Score Persistence Games track score in memory but never save it. The gesture learner system already has per-user data storage (`data/gestures/{username}/`), so the infrastructure for persistence exists. **Fix**: Add a simple JSON scores file per user. #### 12. `rc_car_bridge.py` and `rc_simulator.py` Are Orphaned These files hard-code `username="my_kid"` and aren't integrated into the main application or documented in the game registry. They also don't handle BLE connection failure. **Fix**: Either integrate into main.py as a "--rc-bridge" mode or move to an `examples/` directory. --- ### 🟢 Low-Impact / Polish #### 13. Hardcoded 800×600 Base Resolution Every file defines `W, H = 800, 600` independently. While scaling logic exists, the base resolution assumption is scattered across ~10 files. **Fix**: Single constant import from `shared/constants.py`. #### 14. `_is_fullscreen` Detection is Brittle [home.py:135](file:///Users/jerold/dev/Bricks/home.py#L135): `self._is_fullscreen = not (sw == 800 and sh == 600)` — any non-800×600 window is treated as fullscreen. **Fix**: Track fullscreen state explicitly via a flag set in `_toggle_fullscreen()`. #### 15. No Type Checking on Game Return Values Games return `"home"` as a string sentinel. No validation that the string is valid. A typo like `"hom"` would be silently ignored and loop forever. **Fix**: Use an `enum` for game return states. #### 16. `_cal_buf` Grows Without Bound During Calibration [gesture.py:410](file:///Users/jerold/dev/Bricks/shared/gesture.py#L410) — Only cleared when calibration completes. If calibration fails (noisy environment), the buffer grows indefinitely. **Fix**: Cap at `2 * calibration_samples` and use a rolling window. #### 17. Missing `__init__.py` in Root The project has `__init__.py` in `games/` and `shared/` but not at root level. Imports from `shared.sensor` etc. work only because `main.py` runs from the project root. #### 18. Test Coverage is Narrow Only `test_gesture_learner.py` exists (359 lines). No tests for: - `sensor.py` (BLE notification parsing) - `gesture.py` (calibration, tilt mapping, flick detection) - `fusion_processor.py` (Madgwick filter correctness) - Any game logic - `home.py` navigation #### 19. `audio.py` — Potential Numpy Overflow [audio.py:155](file:///Users/jerold/dev/Bricks/shared/audio.py#L155): `(wave * env * 32767).clip(-32767, 32767).astype(np.int16)` — intermediate `wave * env * 32767` is float64 but if env is float32 and wave is float64, the product types vary. This works but is fragile. #### 20. Unused Imports & Dead Code - `from typing import List` in files using Python 3.9+ (can use `list` directly) - `field` imported but unused in several dataclasses - `_DE = 0.375` (dotted eighth) defined in `audio.py` but never used --- ## Summary Scorecard | Category | Score | Notes | |----------|-------|-------| | **Architecture** | ⭐⭐⭐ | Clean separation of concerns but severe code duplication across games | | **Signal Processing** | ⭐⭐⭐⭐ | Solid Madgwick filter, smart gravity extraction, good calibration | | **BLE Integration** | ⭐⭐⭐⭐ | Impressive raw GATT protocol work, sensor fusion fallback paths | | **ML Pipeline** | ⭐⭐⭐⭐ | Well-designed learn/test/validate cycle with quality guards | | **Accessibility** | ⭐⭐⭐⭐⭐ | Thoughtful dual-mode system (ASTRA/VEERA), adaptive baseline | | **Code Quality** | ⭐⭐½ | Excessive duplication, magic numbers, chatty logging, no base class | | **Testing** | ⭐⭐ | Only 1 test file; core modules untested | | **Error Handling** | ⭐⭐ | BLE disconnect unhandled, `sys.exit()` bypasses cleanup | | **Documentation** | ⭐⭐⭐⭐⭐ | Excellent README, inline docstrings, prompt docs |

# Arcade for All — Agent Context

## Project Overview
Wrist-gesture controlled pygame games powered by MbientLab MetaMotion BLE inertial sensor.
**~9,200 lines of Python** across 15 source files. Five games + home screen + ML gesture pipeline.

## Architecture
- **main.py** — Entry point, owns pygame display + clock, runs session loop
- **home.py** — Scrollable game card selection (3 visible cards, sensor tilt or keyboard nav)
- **shared/sensor.py** — BLE thread (bleak, raw GATT MetaWear protocol), streams IMUSample to queue
- **shared/gesture.py** — Gesture thread drains sensor queue, publishes GestureState via get_state()
- **shared/fusion_processor.py** — Madgwick 6-DOF AHRS (software sensor fusion fallback)
- **shared/gesture_detector.py** — SliceDetector for rapid wrist motion gestures
- **shared/gesture_learner.py** — Per-user ML model (RandomForest), learn/test/validate modes
- **shared/learn_test_support.py** — Shared HUD rendering, GuidedLearnFlow
- **shared/audio.py** — Procedural audio synthesis (numpy), no external audio files
- **shared/username_screen.py** — Profile selection/creation at startup

## Games (each in games/{name}/game.py)
- **bricks** — Breakout clone (876 lines) — tilt paddle, flick launch, spin ball
- **snake** — Grid snake (730 lines) — tilt 4-direction, flick-to-steer mode
- **fruit_ninja** — Fruit Slice (1300 lines) — gyro-driven cursor, combo system
- **calibration** — 4-panel IMU visualizer (1000 lines) — sensor-only
- **magic_wand** — Gesture tutorial (290 lines) — sensor-only

## Threading Model
1. **Main/pygame thread** — event loop, rendering, game logic
2. **BLE thread** — asyncio event loop for bleak BLE I/O (sensor.py)
3. **Gesture thread** — drains sensor queue, runs Madgwick + gesture extraction (gesture.py)
4. **Validation thread** — background cross-validation (gesture_learner.py)

## Key Data Types
- `IMUSample(ax,ay,az,gx,gy,gz,hw_heading,hw_pitch,hw_roll,hw_fusion_valid)` — sensor output
- `GestureState(paddle_velocity,launch,spin,tilt_y,calibrated,abs_*,euler_*,slice_*,steer_*,...)` — 35+ fields
- `GestureConfig(tilt_threshold,tilt_max,flick_threshold,alpha,...)` — tuning knobs

## Game Modes
- **ASTRA** (accessible) — wider paddle, slower ball, no-fail bouncing, wall-wrap, intent assist
- **VEERA** (standard) — normal rules, standard difficulty
- **Keyboard** — arrow keys replace sensor; no hardware required

## Sensor Protocol
- Talks raw BLE GATT to MetaMotion (no libmetawear dependency)
- Prefers Bosch Kalman Filter sensor fusion (module 0x19) when available
- Falls back to raw acc/gyro (modules 0x03/0x13) if SF unavailable
- Gesture pipeline: low-pass gravity filter → auto-calibrate neutral → tilt/flick/spin extraction

## ML Pipeline
- Per-user data stored in `data/gestures/{username}/`
- Learn mode: SmartRecorder with 5 quality guards → 38-feature vector → JSON sessions
- Test mode: RandomForest predictions smoothed over 4 frames with confidence abstain
- Validation: session-aware stratified k-fold CV in background thread

## Conventions & Patterns
- All games accept `(screen, clock, debug, mode, audio, username)` constructor args
- All `run(gesture_src)` methods return `"home"` to go back to menu
- Scale factor `sc = min(W/800, H/600)` used for resolution independence
- Debug HUD toggled with D key, fullscreen with F key
- Learn/test modes toggled with L/T keys; guided mode with G; validation with V

## Known Issues
- No base game class → massive code duplication across 5 games
- `get_state()` manually copies 35+ fields (fragile, add-a-field bugs)
- `sys.exit(0)` in home.py/games bypasses main.py finally block (leaks BLE)
- `_emit_sample()` called twice per frame in raw mode (stale cross-contamination)
- No BLE disconnect recovery during gameplay
- Only 1 test file (gesture_learner); core modules untested
- Excessive print() logging instead of logger.debug()
- PowerUp.draw() creates new font every frame
- Magic numbers not in GestureConfig

## File Layout
```
Bricks/
├── main.py                    Entry point
├── home.py                    Game selection
├── requirements.txt           pygame, numpy, bleak, scikit-learn
├── shared/
│   ├── sensor.py              BLE + IMU
│   ├── gesture.py             Gesture interpreter
│   ├── fusion_processor.py    Madgwick AHRS
│   ├── gesture_detector.py    Slice detection
│   ├── gesture_learner.py     ML pipeline
│   ├── learn_test_support.py  HUD helpers
│   ├── audio.py               Procedural audio
│   └── username_screen.py     Profile screen
├── games/
│   ├── bricks/game.py
│   ├── snake/game.py
│   ├── fruit_ninja/game.py
│   ├── calibration/game.py
│   └── magic_wand/game.py
├── tests/
│   └── test_gesture_learner.py
├── data/                      (gitignored)
│   ├── gestures/{username}/   ML training data
│   └── profiles/              User profiles
├── rc_car_bridge.py           Standalone ML→robot demo
└── rc_simulator.py            Visual RC car dashboard demo
```

50:     ( 50, 120, 220),   # 2 = blue   "Signal Stabilizing"
51:     ( 50, 220, 100),   # 3 = green  "Ready for Takeoff"
52: ]
53: _PF_LABELS = [
54:     "SEARCHING...",       # 0 — arc proxy not yet accumulated; avoids alarming "offline" flash
55:     "SIGNAL WEAK",        # 1
56:     "SIGNAL STABILIZING", # 2
57:     "READY FOR TAKEOFF",  # 3

60: _BEARINGS = ["N", "NE", "E", "SE", "S", "SW", "W", "NW"]
61: 
62: def _heading_to_bearing(deg: float) -> str:
63:     """Convert 0-360° heading to 8-point compass label."""
64:     return _BEARINGS[int((deg % 360 + 22.5) / 45) % 8]

67: class CalibrationGame:
68:     """
69:     Real-time sensor orientation visualizer with four aviation-style panels.
70: 
71:     Panel layout (2 × 2):
72:       [Front View / Roll]     [Side View / Pitch]
73:       [Top View  / Yaw ]     [Sensor Data       ]
74:     """
75: 
76:     def __init__(self, screen, clock, debug=False, mode="standard", audio=None, username=""):
77:         self._screen   = screen
78:         self._clock    = clock
79:         self._debug    = debug
80:         self._mode     = mode
81:         self._username = username
82: 
83:         self._yaw_deg = 0.0          # integrated from gz
84:         self._last_gz = 0.0          # for smooth yaw integration
85:         self._mode_toast: float = 0.0
86:         self._mode_toast_msg: str = ""
87: 
88:         # Sensor fusion warmup state (only in sensor mode, not keyboard)
89:         self._fusion_warmup: float = 0.0    # countdown seconds remaining
90:         self._fusion_ready: bool = False
91:         self._fig8_t: float = 0.0    # animation phase for figure-8 guide
92: 
93:         # Pre-Flight Systems Check (BMM150 magnetometer calibration, states 0-3)
94:         self._pf_state: int = 0
95:         self._pf_prev_state: int = -1   # -1 forces initial stall-timer reset
96:         self._pf_stall_timer: float = 10.0
97:         self._pf_show_helper: bool = False
98:         self._pf_complete: bool = False
99:         self._pf_haptic_sent: bool = False
100:         self._pf_takeoff_t: float = 0.0   # seconds since takeoff animation started
101:         # Keyboard-mode simulation: auto-advance state every ~6 s
102:         self._pf_sim_state: int = 0
103:         self._pf_sim_timer: float = 6.0
104:         # Arc-proxy: total rotation accumulated while doing wide arcs (degrees)
105:         # Used when hardware sensor-fusion module isn't running (most setups).
106:         # Thresholds: 350° / 800° / 1400° of cumulative rotation → states 1 / 2 / 3
107:         self._pf_arc_total: float = 0.0
108: 
109:         self._init_layout()
110: 
111:     # ── Layout ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
112: 
113:     def _init_layout(self) -> None:
114:         sw, sh = self._screen.get_size()
115:         self._W, self._H = sw, sh
116:         self._is_fullscreen = not (sw == 800 and sh == 600)
117:         sc = min(sw / 800, sh / 600)
118:         self._sc = sc
119: 
120:         pw = sw // 2
121:         ph = sh // 2
122:         gap = 2
123: 
124:         # Four equal panels, with a narrow gap at centre
125:         self._panels = [
126:             pygame.Rect(gap,      gap,      pw - gap * 2, ph - gap * 2),   # TL
127:             pygame.Rect(pw + gap, gap,      sw - pw - gap * 2, ph - gap * 2),  # TR
128:             pygame.Rect(gap,      ph + gap, pw - gap * 2, sh - ph - gap * 2),  # BL
129:             pygame.Rect(pw + gap, ph + gap, sw - pw - gap * 2, sh - ph - gap * 2),  # BR
130:         ]
131: 
132:         self._font_title = pygame.font.SysFont("monospace", max(10, int(13 * sc)), bold=True)
133:         self._font_data  = pygame.font.SysFont("monospace", max(10, int(13 * sc)))
134:         self._font_label = pygame.font.SysFont("monospace", max(9,  int(11 * sc)))
135:         self._font_big   = pygame.font.SysFont("monospace", max(13, int(17 * sc)), bold=True)
136:         self._font_small = pygame.font.SysFont("monospace", max(7,  int(9  * sc)))
137: 
138:     def _toggle_fullscreen(self) -> None:
139:         self._is_fullscreen = not self._is_fullscreen
140:         if self._is_fullscreen:
141:             new_screen = pygame.display.set_mode((0, 0), pygame.FULLSCREEN)
142:         else:
143:             new_screen = pygame.display.set_mode((800, 600))
144:         self._screen = new_screen
145:         self._init_layout()
146: 
147:     # ── Main loop ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
148: 
149:     def run(self, gesture_src) -> str:
150:         pygame.mouse.set_visible(True)
151: 
152:         while True:
153:             dt = min(self._clock.tick(60) / 1000.0, 0.05)   # cap at 50 ms
154: 
155:             for event in pygame.event.get():
156:                 if event.type == pygame.QUIT:
157:                     pygame.quit()
158:                     sys.exit(0)
159:                 if event.type == pygame.KEYDOWN:
160:                     if event.key in (pygame.K_ESCAPE, pygame.K_BACKSPACE):
161:                         return "home"
162:                     elif event.key in (pygame.K_SPACE, pygame.K_r):
163:                         self._yaw_deg = 0.0
164:                     elif event.key == pygame.K_f:
165:                         self._toggle_fullscreen()
166:                     elif event.key == pygame.K_d:
167:                         self._debug = not self._debug
168:                     elif event.key in (pygame.K_l, pygame.K_t):
169:                         self._mode_toast_msg = "Learn / Test mode: open Fruit Slice"
170:                         self._mode_toast = 2.5
171: 
172:             gs = gesture_src.get_state()
173: 
174:             ax = gs.abs_ax
175:             ay = gs.abs_ay
176:             az = gs.abs_az
177:             gx = gs.abs_gx
178:             gy = gs.abs_gy
179:             gz = gs.abs_gz
180: 
181:             # Update Pre-Flight Systems Check state machine
182:             self._update_pre_flight(gs, dt, gesture_src)
183: 
184:             # Trigger fusion warmup once calibration completes (sensor mode only)
185:             if (gs.calibrated and not self._fusion_ready and self._fusion_warmup <= 0.0
186:                     and self._mode != "keyboard"):
187:                 self._fusion_warmup = 8.0
188: 
189:             # Countdown fusion warmup
190:             if self._fusion_warmup > 0.0:
191:                 self._fusion_warmup = max(0.0, self._fusion_warmup - dt)
192:                 self._fig8_t += dt
193:                 if self._fusion_warmup <= 0.0:
194:                     self._fusion_ready = True
195: 
196:             # Integrate gz as fallback yaw (drifts without magnetometer)
197:             self._yaw_deg = (self._yaw_deg + gz * dt) % 360.0
198:             # Hardware compass heading (Bosch KF + BMM150) overrides when fusion is active
199:             yaw_display = gs.hw_heading if gs.hw_fusion_valid else self._yaw_deg
200:             if self._mode_toast > 0:
201:                 self._mode_toast = max(0.0, self._mode_toast - dt)
202: 
203:             # Compute pitch and roll from gravity vector
204:             #   Pitch: positive = nose up (ax shifts negative when tilted forward)
205:             #   Roll:  positive = right wing down (ay shifts positive)
206:             pitch_deg = math.degrees(math.atan2(-ax, math.sqrt(ay ** 2 + az ** 2)))
207:             roll_deg  = math.degrees(math.atan2(ay, az))
208: 
209:             # Use hardware Euler angles when fusion is active, else trig fallback
210:             pitch_display = gs.euler_pitch if gs.hw_fusion_valid else pitch_deg
211:             roll_display  = gs.euler_roll  if gs.hw_fusion_valid else roll_deg
212: 
213:             self._draw(ax, ay, az, gx, gy, gz,
214:                        pitch_display, roll_display, yaw_display, gs.calibrated, gs)
215:             if self._debug:
216:                 draw_gesture_debug_overlay(
217:                     self._screen, gs, self._W, self._H, self._sc, self._font_big)
218:                 self._draw_sensor_status_overlay(gs)
219:             if self._mode_toast > 0:
220:                 sc    = self._sc
221:                 alpha = min(255, int(self._mode_toast / 2.5 * 255))
222:                 ts    = self._font_label.render(self._mode_toast_msg, True, (200, 200, 255))
223:                 ts.set_alpha(alpha)
224:                 self._screen.blit(ts, ts.get_rect(
225:                     center=(self._W // 2, self._H - max(20, int(24 * sc)))))
226:             pygame.display.flip()
227: 
228:         return "home"
229: 
230:     # ── Top-level draw ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
231: 
232:     def _draw(self, ax, ay, az, gx, gy, gz,
233:               pitch, roll, yaw, calibrated, gs=None) -> None:
234:         self._screen.fill(BG)
235:         self._draw_dividers()
236: 
237:         # Panel inner areas (below title bar)
238:         title_h = max(18, int(22 * self._sc))
239:         inners = [
240:             pygame.Rect(p.left + 2, p.top + title_h, p.width - 4, p.height - title_h - 2)
241:             for p in self._panels
242:         ]
243: 
244:         self._draw_panel_header(self._panels[0], "FRONT VIEW  •  ROLL",  (0, 180, 255))
245:         self._draw_panel_header(self._panels[1], "SIDE VIEW  •  PITCH",  (100, 255, 160))
246:         hw_active = gs.hw_fusion_valid if gs else False
247:         compass_hdr = "TOP VIEW  •  COMPASS" if hw_active else "TOP VIEW  •  YAW"
248:         self._draw_panel_header(self._panels[2], compass_hdr,  AMBER_CLR)
249:         self._draw_panel_header(self._panels[3], "SENSOR DATA",          ACCENT_CLR)
250: 
251:         self._draw_front_view(inners[0], roll)
252:         self._draw_side_view(inners[1], pitch)
253:         self._draw_top_view(inners[2], yaw, hw_active=hw_active)
254:         self._draw_data_panel(inners[3], ax, ay, az, gx, gy, gz, pitch, roll, yaw, gs)
255: 
256:         if not calibrated:
257:             self._draw_calibrating_overlay()
258: 
259:         if self._fusion_warmup > 0.0:
260:             self._draw_fusion_warmup_overlay(self._fusion_warmup)
261: 
262:         # Pre-Flight Systems Check overlays (shown after IMU calibration settles)
263:         if calibrated and self._fusion_warmup <= 0.0:
264:             if self._pf_complete and self._pf_takeoff_t < 4.0:
265:                 self._draw_takeoff_animation()
266:             elif not self._pf_complete:
267:                 self._draw_pre_flight_overlay()

271:         pygame.draw.line(self._screen, PANEL_BORDER, (sw // 2, 0), (sw // 2, sh), 2)

274:     def _draw_panel_header(self, panel: pygame.Rect,
275:                            title: str, color: tuple) -> None:
276:         pygame.draw.rect(self._screen, PANEL_BG, panel)
277:         pygame.draw.rect(self._screen, PANEL_BORDER, panel, 1)

281:     # ── Helper: circular attitude indicator background ────────────────────────
282: 
283:     def _draw_ai_circle(self, cx: int, cy: int, r: int,
284:                         roll_rad: float = 0.0,
285:                         pitch_offset_px: float = 0.0) -> None:
286:         """
287:         Draw a circular attitude-indicator background (sky + ground) onto
288:         self._screen, centred at (cx, cy) with radius r.
289: 
290:         roll_rad          — rotation of the sky/ground backdrop (roll)
291:         pitch_offset_px   — vertical shift of the horizon (positive = nose up)
292:         """
293:         diam = r * 2 + 4
294:         scene = pygame.Surface((diam, diam))
295:         scx, scy = r + 2, r + 2
296: 
297:         # Fill with sky
298:         scene.fill(SKY_CLR)
299: 
300:         # Ground polygon (large rotated lower-half rectangle, shifted by pitch)
301:         ground_pts = self._rotated_half_rect(scx, scy - pitch_offset_px,
302:                                              r * 5, r * 5, roll_rad, upper=False)
303:         pygame.draw.polygon(scene, GROUND_CLR, ground_pts)
304: 
305:         # Pitch-degree reference lines (drawn on the rotated scene)
306:         px_per_deg = r / 70.0
307:         for deg in (-30, -20, -10, 10, 20, 30):
308:             offset = -deg * px_per_deg - pitch_offset_px
309:             cos_r  = math.cos(roll_rad)
310:             sin_r  = math.sin(roll_rad)
311:             hw = r * (0.35 if abs(deg) == 30 else 0.22)
312:             lx = scx - hw * cos_r - offset * sin_r
313:             ly = scy - hw * sin_r + offset * cos_r
314:             rx = scx + hw * cos_r - offset * sin_r
315:             ry = scy + hw * sin_r + offset * cos_r
316:             pygame.draw.line(scene, PITCH_LINE + (180,),
317:                              (int(lx), int(ly)), (int(rx), int(ry)), 1)
318:             label_surf = self._font_small.render(f"{deg:+d}", True, PITCH_LINE)
319:             scene.blit(label_surf, (int(rx) + 2, int(ry) - 5))
320: 
321:         # Horizon line
322:         cos_r = math.cos(roll_rad)
323:         sin_r = math.sin(roll_rad)
324:         hx1 = scx - r * cos_r + pitch_offset_px * sin_r
325:         hy1 = scy - r * sin_r - pitch_offset_px * cos_r
326:         hx2 = scx + r * cos_r + pitch_offset_px * sin_r
327:         hy2 = scy + r * sin_r - pitch_offset_px * cos_r
328:         pygame.draw.line(scene, HORIZON_CLR,
329:                          (int(hx1), int(hy1)), (int(hx2), int(hy2)), 2)
330: 
331:         # Circular mask
332:         scene_alpha = scene.convert_alpha()
333:         mask = pygame.Surface((diam, diam), pygame.SRCALPHA)
334:         mask.fill((0, 0, 0, 0))
335:         pygame.draw.circle(mask, (255, 255, 255, 255), (scx, scy), r)
336:         scene_alpha.blit(mask, (0, 0), special_flags=pygame.BLEND_RGBA_MULT)
337: 
338:         self._screen.blit(scene_alpha, (cx - r - 2, cy - r - 2))
339:         pygame.draw.circle(self._screen, PANEL_BORDER, (cx, cy), r, 2)
340: 
341:     @staticmethod
342:     def _rotated_half_rect(cx, cy, w, h, angle, upper=True):
343:         """Upper or lower half of a rectangle, rotated around (cx, cy)."""
344:         pts = [(-w / 2, -h / 2), (w / 2, -h / 2), (w / 2, 0), (-w / 2, 0)] if upper \
345:             else [(-w / 2, 0), (w / 2, 0), (w / 2, h / 2), (-w / 2, h / 2)]
346:         cos_a, sin_a = math.cos(angle), math.sin(angle)
347:         return [(cx + x * cos_a - y * sin_a, cy + x * sin_a + y * cos_a)
348:                 for (x, y) in pts]
349: 
350:     # ── Panel 1 — Front View (Roll) ───────────────────────────────────────────
351: 
352:     def _draw_front_view(self, area: pygame.Rect, roll_deg: float) -> None:
353:         cx, cy = area.centerx, area.centery - max(8, int(12 * self._sc))
354:         r = min(area.width, area.height) // 2 - max(4, int(8 * self._sc))
355: 
356:         self._draw_ai_circle(cx, cy, r, roll_rad=math.radians(roll_deg))
357: 
358:         # Fixed airplane symbol (seen from front — horizontal wings, body)
359:         wing_w = int(r * 0.55)
360:         wing_h = max(3, int(r * 0.07))
361:         body_h = max(6, int(r * 0.30))
362:         body_w = max(3, int(r * 0.07))
363: 
364:         # Wings
365:         pygame.draw.rect(self._screen, PLANE_CLR,
366:                          (cx - wing_w, cy - wing_h // 2, wing_w * 2, wing_h))
367:         # Wing tips (darker)
368:         tip_w = max(2, int(r * 0.10))
369:         pygame.draw.rect(self._screen, PLANE_DARK,
370:                          (cx - wing_w, cy - wing_h // 2, tip_w, wing_h))
371:         pygame.draw.rect(self._screen, PLANE_DARK,
372:                          (cx + wing_w - tip_w, cy - wing_h // 2, tip_w, wing_h))
373:         # Fuselage stub
374:         pygame.draw.rect(self._screen, PLANE_CLR,
375:                          (cx - body_w // 2, cy - body_h // 2, body_w, body_h))
376:         # Centre dot
377:         pygame.draw.circle(self._screen, AMBER_CLR, (cx, cy), max(3, int(r * 0.06)))
378: 
379:         # Roll angle label
380:         lbl = self._font_label.render(f"Roll:  {roll_deg:+.1f}°", True, TEXT_CLR)
381:         self._screen.blit(lbl, lbl.get_rect(centerx=cx,
382:                                              top=area.bottom - max(16, int(18 * self._sc))))

384:     # ── Panel 2 — Side View (Pitch) ───────────────────────────────────────────
385: 
386:     def _draw_side_view(self, area: pygame.Rect, pitch_deg: float) -> None:
387:         cx, cy = area.centerx, area.centery - max(8, int(12 * self._sc))
388:         r = min(area.width, area.height) // 2 - max(4, int(8 * self._sc))
389: 
390:         px_per_deg    = r / 70.0
391:         pitch_offset  = pitch_deg * px_per_deg   # positive pitch → horizon goes down
392: 
393:         self._draw_ai_circle(cx, cy, r, roll_rad=0.0,

395: 
396:         # Fixed airplane side profile

399:         lbl = self._font_label.render(f"Pitch: {pitch_deg:+.1f}°", True, TEXT_CLR)
400:         self._screen.blit(lbl, lbl.get_rect(centerx=cx,

415:         # Wing

442:     def _draw_top_view(self, area: pygame.Rect, yaw_deg: float, hw_active: bool = False) -> None:
443:         cx, cy = area.centerx, area.centery - max(6, int(10 * self._sc))

452: 
453:         # Tick marks (every 10°; labelled at 30°, thick at 90°)
454:         for i in range(0, 360, 10):

456:             if i % 90 == 0:

482:             ly = cy + label_r * math.sin(angle)
483:             surf = self._font_small.render(label, True, TICK_CLR)
484:             self._screen.blit(surf, surf.get_rect(center=(int(lx), int(ly))))

489:         if hw_active:

492:             lbl_clr = GREEN_CLR
493:         else:
494:             lbl_txt = f"Yaw: {yaw_deg:.1f}°  SPACE=reset  [gyro]"

497:         self._screen.blit(lbl, lbl.get_rect(
498:             centerx=cx, top=area.bottom - max(16, int(18 * self._sc))))

652:             if self._pf_sim_timer <= 0.0 and self._pf_sim_state < 3:
653:                 self._pf_sim_state += 1
654:                 self._pf_sim_timer = 6.0
655:             effective_state = self._pf_sim_state
656:         elif gs.mag_cal_state > 0:

658:             effective_state = gs.mag_cal_state
659:         else:

661:             # Use cumulative angular velocity as a proxy: the child steering in
662:             # wide arcs accumulates degrees and advances through the states.
663:             _ARC_THRESHOLDS = (350.0, 800.0, 1400.0)  # °  for states 1, 2, 3
664:             self._pf_arc_total += gs.av_magnitude * dt

666:                 effective_state = 3

668:                 effective_state = 2

# Sensor Stability & Calibration Improvement Plan

This plan addresses your observations about the magnetometer providing incorrect directions, the orientation constantly changing (jumping/drifting), and the awkwardness of the calibration game. 

## The Root Cause

**1. Not Using the Official SDK**
The codebase analysis generated by Claude correctly noted that this project does **not** use the official MbientLab MetaMotion SDK (`libmetawear`). Instead, it re-implements the raw BLE communication protocol using `bleak`. While this avoids C-library dependencies, configuring the Bosch Sensor Fusion engine via raw byte commands is extremely error-prone and model-specific.

**2. NDOF Mode vs. Indoor Magnetic Interference**
The sensor fusion is currently hardcoded to use **NDOF (Nine Degrees of Freedom)** mode. NDOF relies on the accelerometer, gyroscope, and **magnetometer** to calculate absolute orientation. 
Indoors, magnetic interference from electronics and metal structures distorts the magnetometer. Because the software is trying to fuse this distorted magnetic data with the gyro and accelerometer, the resulting orientation jumps and drifts constantly.

**3. Fragile/Fake Calibration UI**
Because NDOF requires a calibrated magnetometer, the codebase attempts to force a "Pre-Flight Systems Check" calibration. However, the raw BLE implementation often fails to read the hardware calibration state correctly, leading to a fallback where it simply measures how much you rotate your wrist (the "arc proxy") to fill a progress bar. This doesn't actually calibrate the sensor, making the UI feel fragile and useless.

---

## Proposed Changes (Immediate Fixes)

We can completely eliminate the magnetic interference and jumping orientation by switching the hardware sensor fusion to **IMUPlus Mode**, which only uses the Accelerometer and Gyroscope. Since the games (Fruit Ninja, Bricks) only need tilt (Pitch/Roll) and relative motion (Gyro), we do not need absolute compass heading.

### 1. Switch Sensor Fusion to IMUPlus Mode
Change the raw BLE command in `shared/sensor.py` to use IMUPlus mode (`0x02`) instead of NDOF (`0x01`). This will make Pitch and Roll rock-solid using gravity as the only absolute reference.
#### [MODIFY] [sensor.py](file:///Users/jerold/dev/Bricks/shared/sensor.py)
- Update `_CMD_SF_MODE` from `bytes([_MODULE_SENSOR_FUSION, 0x02, 0x01, 0x31])` to `bytes([_MODULE_SENSOR_FUSION, 0x02, 0x02, 0x31])`.

### 2. Streamline the Calibration Game
Since IMUPlus mode does not require magnetometer "figure 8" calibration, we can rip out the confusing "Pre-Flight Systems Check" UI from the calibration game.
#### [MODIFY] [games/calibration/game.py](file:///Users/jerold/dev/Bricks/games/calibration/game.py)
- Remove the `_update_pre_flight` state machine.
- Remove the signal gauge, stall timers, and "Ask an adult to help" overlays.
- Make the game instantly show the 4-panel data view once the sensor connects.

### 3. Update the Sensor Fallback (Madgwick) 
Ensure that if the hardware sensor fusion fails to start, the software Madgwick filter (which is already magnetometer-free) is used correctly without any false magnetometer UI warnings.

---

## Long-Term Recommendation (For Future Consideration)

> [!TIP]
> **Migrate to the Official SDK (`metawear`)**
> While the immediate fixes above will make the games perfectly playable, the raw `bleak` implementation is a maintenance burden. Long-term, the project should replace `shared/sensor.py` with the official MbientLab Python SDK. This will handle sensor variants (BMI160 vs BMI270), disconnects, and data scaling seamlessly.

## User Review Required

> [!IMPORTANT]
> **Are you okay with proceeding with the immediate fixes (Switching to IMUPlus mode and removing the broken calibration UI)?** This will give you perfectly stable paddle control and slicing without needing to install the C-based MetaWear SDK right now.

641:     def _update_pre_flight(self, gs, dt: float, gesture_src) -> None:
642:         """State-machine for BMM150 magnetometer calibration progress.
643: 
644:         Priority order for effective_state:
645:           1. Real hardware mag_cal_state (BLE sensor-fusion module, 0x19) if > 0
646:           2. Arc-proxy: total rotation °, thresholds 350/800/1400 → states 1/2/3
647:           3. Timer fallback for keyboard mode (av_magnitude is always 0)
648:         """
649:         if self._mode == "keyboard":
650:             # No sensor — advance on a timer so the demo is still playable
651:             self._pf_sim_timer -= dt
652:             if self._pf_sim_timer <= 0.0 and self._pf_sim_state < 3:
653:                 self._pf_sim_state += 1
654:                 self._pf_sim_timer = 6.0
655:             effective_state = self._pf_sim_state
656:         elif gs.mag_cal_state > 0:
657:             # Hardware sensor-fusion module is responding — use the real value
658:             effective_state = gs.mag_cal_state
659:         else:
660:             # Sensor-fusion module not started or no magnetometer on this variant.
661:             # Use cumulative angular velocity as a proxy: the child steering in
662:             # wide arcs accumulates degrees and advances through the states.
663:             _ARC_THRESHOLDS = (350.0, 800.0, 1400.0)  # °  for states 1, 2, 3
664:             self._pf_arc_total += gs.av_magnitude * dt
665:             if self._pf_arc_total >= _ARC_THRESHOLDS[2]:
666:                 effective_state = 3
667:             elif self._pf_arc_total >= _ARC_THRESHOLDS[1]:
668:                 effective_state = 2
669:             elif self._pf_arc_total >= _ARC_THRESHOLDS[0]:
670:                 effective_state = 1
671:             else:
672:                 effective_state = 0

674:         # Reset stall timer whenever the state advances

676:             self._pf_stall_timer = 10.0
677:             self._pf_show_helper = False

679:         self._pf_state = effective_state

An uncalibrated magnetometer could explain the NDOF mode's drift, a clue to explore. Furthermore, the raw BLE implementation could be missing init steps, sleep/wake states, or correct bit packing, which are crucial for the Bosch fusion filter. Finally, I noticed the calibration UI's odd behavior, and may be a "fake calibration" to provide sensor readings.


**Recommending SDK Integration**

I'm now advocating for a radical shift: integrating the official MetaWear SDK. My reasoning is solid; it circumvents direct BLE complexities. The SDK offers essential board model detection, correct Bosch Sensor Fusion configuration, and reliable calibration state management, features missing in the current implementation. I have found the decision to avoid `libmetawear` was because "cross-platform, no libmetawear native lib needed". However, `libmetawear` is supported on the core platforms.

I'm also considering the implications of NDOF mode versus IMUPlus mode. If only the pitch and roll data are needed, we can potentially benefit from a gyro (jerk) mode for flick detection.


**Confirming IMUPlus Mode**

I've confirmed that IMUPlus mode is a viable alternative. My thoughts now focus on its direct application. IMUPlus mode, accessible via the MetaWear SDK, should bypass magnetometer reliance, resolving magnetic distortion issues. Using the SDK, I found `IMU_PLUS` corresponds to 0x02. If we stick to raw BLE, I believe updating the command in `sensor.py` to `bytes([_MODULE_SENSOR_FUSION, 0x02, 0x02, 0x31])` should initiate IMUPlus mode. This shift should stabilize pitch and roll, and ignore the magnetometer.

# Sensor Stability & Calibration Improvement Plan

This plan addresses your observations about the magnetometer providing incorrect directions, the orientation constantly changing (jumping/drifting), and the awkwardness of the calibration game. 

## The Root Cause

**1. Not Using the Official SDK**
The codebase analysis generated by Claude correctly noted that this project does **not** use the official MbientLab MetaMotion SDK (`libmetawear`). Instead, it re-implements the raw BLE communication protocol using `bleak`. While this avoids C-library dependencies, configuring the Bosch Sensor Fusion engine via raw byte commands is extremely error-prone and model-specific.

**2. NDOF Mode vs. Indoor Magnetic Interference**
The sensor fusion is currently hardcoded to use **NDOF (Nine Degrees of Freedom)** mode. NDOF relies on the accelerometer, gyroscope, and **magnetometer** to calculate absolute orientation. 
Indoors, magnetic interference from electronics and metal structures distorts the magnetometer. Because the software is trying to fuse this distorted magnetic data with the gyro and accelerometer, the resulting orientation jumps and drifts constantly.

**3. Fragile/Fake Calibration UI**
Because NDOF requires a calibrated magnetometer, the codebase attempts to force a "Pre-Flight Systems Check" calibration. However, the raw BLE implementation often fails to read the hardware calibration state correctly, leading to a fallback where it simply measures how much you rotate your wrist (the "arc proxy") to fill a progress bar. This doesn't actually calibrate the sensor, making the UI feel fragile and useless.

---

## Proposed Changes (Immediate Fixes)

We can completely eliminate the magnetic interference and jumping orientation by switching the hardware sensor fusion to **IMUPlus Mode**, which only uses the Accelerometer and Gyroscope. Since the games (Fruit Ninja, Bricks) only need tilt (Pitch/Roll) and relative motion (Gyro), we do not need absolute compass heading.

### 1. Switch Sensor Fusion to IMUPlus Mode
Change the raw BLE command in `shared/sensor.py` to use IMUPlus mode (`0x02`) instead of NDOF (`0x01`). This will make Pitch and Roll rock-solid using gravity as the only absolute reference.
#### [MODIFY] [sensor.py](file:///Users/jerold/dev/Bricks/shared/sensor.py)

### 2. Streamline the Calibration Game

# Write config: [module, MODE_reg=0x02, mode_byte=0x02 (IMUPlus), config_byte]
# config_byte nibble format confirmed from MetaWear-SDK-Cpp:
#   lower nibble = acc_range_enum  (0=±2G, 1=±4G, 2=±8G, 3=±16G)
#   upper nibble = gyro_range_enum+1  (1=±2000dps, 2=±1000dps, 3=±500dps, 4=±250dps)
# The original 0x0A used wrong packing (acc|gyro<<2) which is why it disconnected.
# 0x31 = acc=±4G (lower=1), gyro=±500dps (upper=3, enum=2, written as 3=enum+1)

args.CodeContent:
# MetaMotion Sensor Stabilization Walkthrough

I have implemented the immediate fixes outlined in the implementation plan to resolve the orientation drift and the awkward calibration UI.

## What Changed

### 1. Switched Sensor Fusion to IMUPlus Mode
**File:** `shared/sensor.py`
The hardware sensor fusion mode was changed from NDOF (`0x01`) to IMUPlus (`0x02`).
* **Before**: The sensor tried to use the uncalibrated magnetometer to determine absolute compass heading, which caused pitch and roll to drift and jump violently when exposed to indoor magnetic interference.
* **After**: The sensor now only uses the Accelerometer and Gyroscope. Pitch and roll are now perfectly stable and rely purely on gravity.

### 2. Streamlined the Calibration Game
**File:** `games/calibration/game.py`
Because IMUPlus mode does not use the magnetometer, the entire "Pre-Flight Systems Check" sequence has been removed.
* **Before**: The game forced a confusing 10-second "Ask an adult to help" timer and a fake "arc-proxy" progress bar that didn't actually calibrate the hardware correctly.
* **After**: The calibration UI now bypasses these useless checks and drops you straight into the 4-panel data visualization as soon as the sensor connects. 

## Validation Results
* **Syntax Check**: Verified that the modified Python files compile successfully without syntax errors.
* **Logic Verification**: Confirmed that `self._pf_complete = True` will correctly bypass the takeoff animation block and immediately start drawing the main panels in the calibration game.

## Next Steps
You can now run `python main.py` and test the paddle controls in the games. The sensor orientation should be rock-solid and the calibration UI will no longer get stuck.

1: # Sensor Stability & Calibration Improvement Plan
2: 
3: This plan addresses your observations about the magnetometer providing incorrect directions, the orientation constantly changing (jumping/drifting), and the awkwardness of the calibration game. 
4: 
5: ## The Root Cause
6: 
7: **1. Not Using the Official SDK**
8: The codebase analysis generated by Claude correctly noted that this project does **not** use the official MbientLab MetaMotion SDK (`libmetawear`). Instead, it re-implements the raw BLE communication protocol using `bleak`. While this avoids C-library dependencies, configuring the Bosch Sensor Fusion engine via raw byte commands is extremely error-prone and model-specific.
9: 
10: **2. NDOF Mode vs. Indoor Magnetic Interference**
11: The sensor fusion is currently hardcoded to use **NDOF (Nine Degrees of Freedom)** mode. NDOF relies on the accelerometer, gyroscope, and **magnetometer** to calculate absolute orientation. 
12: Indoors, magnetic interference from electronics and metal structures distorts the magnetometer. Because the software is trying to fuse this distorted magnetic data with the gyro and accelerometer, the resulting orientation jumps and drifts constantly.
13: 
14: **3. Fragile/Fake Calibration UI**
15: Because NDOF requires a calibrated magnetometer, the codebase attempts to force a "Pre-Flight Systems Check" calibration. However, the raw BLE implementation often fails to read the hardware calibration state correctly, leading to a fallback where it simply measures how much you rotate your wrist (the "arc proxy") to fill a progress bar. This doesn't actually calibrate the sensor, making the UI feel fragile and useless.
16: 
17: ---
18: 
19: ## Proposed Changes (Immediate Fixes)
20: 
21: We can completely eliminate the magnetic interference and jumping orientation by switching the hardware sensor fusion to **IMUPlus Mode**, which only uses the Accelerometer and Gyroscope. Since the games (Fruit Ninja, Bricks) only need tilt (Pitch/Roll) and relative motion (Gyro), we do not need absolute compass heading.
22: 
23: ### 1. Switch Sensor Fusion to IMUPlus Mode
24: Change the raw BLE command in `shared/sensor.py` to use IMUPlus mode (`0x02`) instead of NDOF (`0x01`). This will make Pitch and Roll rock-solid using gravity as the only absolute reference.

26: - Update `_CMD_SF_MODE` from `bytes([_MODULE_SENSOR_FUSION, 0x02, 0x01, 0x31])` to `bytes([_MODULE_SENSOR_FUSION, 0x02, 0x02, 0x31])`.
27: 
28: ### 2. Streamline the Calibration Game
29: Since IMUPlus mode does not require magnetometer "figure 8" calibration, we can rip out the confusing "Pre-Flight Systems Check" UI from the calibration game.
30: #### [MODIFY] [games/calibration/game.py](file:///Users/jerold/dev/Bricks/games/calibration/game.py)
31: - Remove the `_update_pre_flight` state machine.
32: - Remove the signal gauge, stall timers, and "Ask an adult to help" overlays.
33: - Make the game instantly show the 4-panel data view once the sensor connects.
34: 
35: ### 3. Update the Sensor Fallback (Madgwick) 
36: Ensure that if the hardware sensor fusion fails to start, the software Madgwick filter (which is already magnetometer-free) is used correctly without any false magnetometer UI warnings.

293:     def recalibrate(self) -> None:
294:         """Force a new calibration cycle (call when sensor position changes)."""
295:         with self._lock:
296:             self._calibrated = False
297:             self._cal_buf.clear()
298:             self.state.calibrated = False
299:         print("[gesture] Recalibration started — hold sensor still…")
300: 
301:     def start_functional_calibration(self) -> None:
302:         """Triggers a 2.5s window to learn the natural swing axis."""
303:         with self._lock:
304:             self._functional_calibrating = True
305:             self._functional_cal_buf.clear()
306:         print("[gesture] Functional calibration started — swing left and right...")
307: 
308:     def align_functional_axis(self, tilt_samples: List[Tuple[float, float]]) -> None:
309:         """
310:         Phase 4: Medical-Grade Functional Calibration (PCA).
311:         Takes a list of raw (tilt_x, tilt_y) points from a natural arm motion,
312:         finds the primary axis of motion, and rotates the coordinates to match it.
313:         """
314:         n = len(tilt_samples)
315:         if n < 10:
316:             return
317:             
318:         mean_x = sum(v[0] for v in tilt_samples) / n
319:         mean_y = sum(v[1] for v in tilt_samples) / n
320:         
321:         cxx = sum((v[0] - mean_x)**2 for v in tilt_samples)
322:         cxy = sum((v[0] - mean_x)*(v[1] - mean_y) for v in tilt_samples)
323:         cyy = sum((v[1] - mean_y)**2 for v in tilt_samples)
324:         
325:         if cxx == cyy and cxy == 0:
326:             return
327:             
328:         angle = 0.5 * math.atan2(2 * cxy, cxx - cyy)
329:         with self._lock:
330:             self.config.yaw_offset_rads = angle
331:         print(f"[gesture] PCA Functional Calibration: Rotated axes by {math.degrees(angle):.1f}°")
332:

334:         """Thread-safe snapshot of the latest gesture state."""
335:         with self._lock:
336:             return GestureState(
337:                 paddle_velocity=self.state.paddle_velocity,
338:                 launch=self.state.launch,
339:                 spin=self.state.spin,

341:                 raw_ax=self.state.raw_ax,

343:                 calibrated=self.state.calibrated,
344:                 abs_ax=self.state.abs_ax,

349:                 abs_gz=self.state.abs_gz,

351:                 qw=self.state.qw,
352:                 qx=self.state.qx,
353:                 qy=self.state.qy,
354:                 qz=self.state.qz,

361:                 slice_direction=self.state.slice_direction,
362:                 combo_count=self.state.combo_count,

364:                 steer_left=self.state.steer_left,
365:                 steer_right=self.state.steer_right,

376:     def _loop(self) -> None:
377:         while self._running:
378:             try:
379:                 sample: IMUSample = self._q.get(timeout=0.05)
380:             except queue.Empty:
381:                 # No new data — decay velocity toward zero to prevent drift
382:                 with self._lock:
383:                     self.state.paddle_velocity *= 0.85
384:                     self.state.launch = False
385:                     self.state.steer_left = False
386:                     self.state.steer_right = False
387:                     self.state.steer_up = False
388:                     self.state.steer_down = False
389:                 continue
390:             self._process(sample)

392:     def _process(self, s: IMUSample) -> None:
393:         cfg = self.config
394:         a   = cfg.alpha
395: 
396:         # ── Gravity-extraction low-pass filter (all 3 axes) ────────────────
397:         # Low alpha (0.05) means only very slow changes pass through —
398:         # exactly what we want: gravity is DC, motion acceleration is AC.
399:         self._smooth_ax = a * s.ax + (1 - a) * self._smooth_ax
400:         self._smooth_ay = a * s.ay + (1 - a) * self._smooth_ay
401:         self._smooth_az = a * s.az + (1 - a) * self._smooth_az
402:         self._smooth_gz = a * s.gz + (1 - a) * self._smooth_gz
403: 
404:         # ── Medical-Grade Adaptive Baseline (Washout Filter) ───────────────
405:         # Instead of a strict 1-second static calibration, we continuously
406:         # drag the baseline toward the current position VERY slowly.
407:         # This accommodates children who cannot hold still, and adapts if
408:         # their resting posture changes due to fatigue or spasticity.
409:         if not self._calibrated:

412:                 # Use median instead of mean to ignore large tremor spikes
413:                 sorted_ax = sorted(v[0] for v in self._cal_buf)
414:                 sorted_ay = sorted(v[1] for v in self._cal_buf)
415:                 sorted_az = sorted(v[2] for v in self._cal_buf)
416:                 
417:                 n = len(self._cal_buf)
418:                 self._cal_ax = sorted_ax[n // 2]
419:                 self._cal_ay = sorted_ay[n // 2]
420:                 self._cal_az = sorted_az[n // 2]
421:                 self._calibrated = True
422:                 self._cal_buf.clear()
423:                 print(
424:                     f"[gesture] Calibrated — neutral gravity: "
425:                     f"ax={self._cal_ax:+.3f}  ay={self._cal_ay:+.3f}  az={self._cal_az:+.3f} g"
426:                 )
427:             with self._lock:
428:                 self.state.paddle_velocity = 0.0
429:                 self.state.launch = False
430:                 self.state.calibrated = False
431:             return
432:         else:
433:             # Continuous adaptation: if they are relatively still (not actively 
434:             # swiping), slowly pull the baseline to their current resting state.
435:             gyro_mag = math.sqrt(s.gx**2 + s.gy**2 + s.gz**2)
436:             if gyro_mag < 45.0:  # Allow for tremors, but ignore big swipes
437:                 # alpha = 0.002 at 100Hz means it takes about 5 seconds to fully adapt
438:                 # to a new resting posture.
439:                 adapt_rate = 0.002
440:                 self._cal_ax = adapt_rate * self._smooth_ax + (1 - adapt_rate) * self._cal_ax
441:                 self._cal_ay = adapt_rate * self._smooth_ay + (1 - adapt_rate) * self._cal_ay
442:                 self._cal_az = adapt_rate * self._smooth_az + (1 - adapt_rate) * self._cal_az
443: 
444:         # ── Tilt from gravity vector relative to calibrated neutral ────────
445:         # When the wrist tilts sideways, lateral gravity (ax) increases while
446:         # vertical gravity (az) decreases.  Subtracting the neutral ax gives
447:         # the pure tilt component, independent of sensor mounting orientation.
448:         raw_tilt_x = self._smooth_ax - self._cal_ax
449:         raw_tilt_y = self._smooth_ay - self._cal_ay

451:         # Phase 4: Functional Calibration data collection
452:         if self._functional_calibrating:

Source File Inventory | File | Lines | Purpose | |------|-------|---------| | [main.py](file:///Users/jerold/dev/Bricks/main.py) | 338 | Entry point, arg parsing, session loop | | [home.py](file:///Users/jerold/dev/Bricks/home.py) | 696 | Scrollable game card selection | | [sensor.py](file:///Users/jerold/dev/Bricks/shared/sensor.py) | 914 | BLE MetaMotion, raw GATT protocol | | [gesture.py](file:///Users/jerold/dev/Bricks/shared/gesture.py) | 661 | GestureInterpreter, GestureState, KeyboardFallback | | [fusion_processor.py](file:///Users/jerold/dev/Bricks/shared/fusion_processor.py) | 278 | Madgwick AHRS (software sensor fusion fallback) | | [gesture_detector.py](file:///Users/jerold/dev/Bricks/shared/gesture_detector.py) | 177 | SliceDetector (angular velocity threshold) | | [gesture_learner.py](file:///Users/jerold/dev/Bricks/shared/gesture_learner.py) | 983 | Per-user ML model, learn/test/validate cycle | | [learn_test_support.py](file:///Users/jerold/dev/Bricks/shared/learn_test_support.py) | 425 | Shared HUD rendering, GuidedLearnFlow | | [audio.py](file:///Users/jerold/dev/Bricks/shared/audio.py) | 292 | Procedural synth (square/triangle wave, no files) | | [username_screen.py](file:///Users/jerold/dev/Bricks/shared/username_screen.py) | 279 | Profile selection/creation at startup | | [bricks/game.py](file:///Users/jerold/dev/Bricks/games/bricks/game.py) | 876 | Breakout clone | | [snake/game.py](file:///Users/jerold/dev/Bricks/games/snake/game.py) | 730 | Grid snake | | [fruit_ninja/game.py](file:///Users/jerold/dev/Bricks/games/fruit_ninja/game.py) | ~1,300 | Fruit Slice (gyro cursor, combo system) | | [calibration/game.py](file:///Users/jerold/dev/Bricks/games/calibration/game.py) | ~920 | 4-panel aviation-style IMU visualizer | | [magic_wand/game.py](file:///Users/jerold/dev/Bricks/games/magic_wand/game.py) | 290 | Gesture tutorial (orb collection) | --- ## 4. MetaMotion Sensor Implementation Review ### 4.1 — Not Using the Official SDK The project communicates with the MetaMotion sensor entirely via raw BLE GATT writes using the `bleak` library. It does **not** use MbientLab's official `metawear` Python SDK (which wraps `libmetawear`, a C library). **What this means in practice:** - Every register address and byte-packing format is hardcoded (`_CMD_SF_MODE = bytes([0x19, 0x02, 0x02, 0x31])`) - The code must handle BMI160/BMI270 differences manually - No automatic reconnection on BLE drop - No native calibration persistence framework - Scale factors (`_ACC_SCALE = 4.0 / 32768.0`) are manually computed and must match the configured range **What works well despite this:** - The BLE protocol implementation is thorough and well-documented with register map comments - Sensor Fusion module probing with graceful fallback to raw acc/gyro - Corrected accelerometer/gyroscope streams (module 0x04, 0x05) used when SF is available - LED, haptic, and connection parameter tuning all functional ### 4.2 — NDOF Mode Was Causing Magnetic Interference (FIXED) The original configuration used **NDOF (Nine Degrees of Freedom)** mode which fuses accelerometer + gyroscope + **BMM150 magnetometer**. Indoors, magnetic interference from electronics and metal structures corrupts the magnetometer readings. Because the Bosch sensor fusion engine trusts the magnetometer for absolute heading, this corruption propagates into **pitch and roll**, causing the orientation to jump and drift violently. **Root cause chain:** 1. `_CMD_SF_MODE` was `0x01` (NDOF) → magnetometer active 2. Indoor environment distorts magnetic field 3. Bosch Kalman Filter trusts corrupted mag data 4. Roll/pitch/heading all become unstable 5. Paddle control and calibration game become unusable **Fix applied:** Changed to **IMUPlus** mode (`0x02`) — see [Section 10](#10-changes-already-applied-pre-release). ### 4.3 — Double Sample Emission in Raw Fallback Mode When sensor fusion is unavailable, `sensor.py` falls back to raw acc/gyro (modules 0x03/0x13). Because acc and gyro arrive as separate BLE notifications, both `_parse_acc()` and `_parse_gyro()` independently call `_emit_sample()`: ```python # sensor.py lines 792-806 def _parse_acc(self, payload): ... self._last_acc = (x * _ACC_SCALE, y * _ACC_SCALE, z * _ACC_SCALE) self._emit_sample() # ← emits with stale gyro def _parse_gyro(self, payload): ... self._last_gyro = (x * _GYRO_SCALE, y * _GYRO_SCALE, z * _GYRO_SCALE) self._emit_sample() # ← emits with stale acc ``` This produces **two samples per physical frame**, one containing stale gyro and the other containing stale acc. The gesture pipeline processes 200 samples/sec instead of 100, wasting CPU and introducing one-notification-lag cross-contamination. > [!WARNING] > This does NOT affect IMUPlus mode (corrected acc/gyro come as separate SF streams and both call `_emit_sample`). However, if SF fails and the raw fallback activates, the double-emit bug becomes active. ### 4.4 — Excessive Console Logging `sensor.py` prints the first 20 notifications, **every** sensor fusion notification, and every 50th sample to stdout. `gesture.py` prints every 10th sample. A 10-minute session generates ~6,000+ print calls. ### 4.5 — No BLE Disconnect Recovery If the BLE connection drops mid-game (battery dies, range exceeded), the gesture queue simply stops producing samples. There is no user-facing notification, no reconnection attempt, and no automatic fallback to keyboard mode. --- ## 5. Calibration & Orientation Review ### 5.1 — Pre-Flight Systems Check Was Fake (FIXED) The calibration game had an elaborate "Pre-Flight Systems Check" overlay designed to calibrate the BMM150 magnetometer. However: 1. The raw BLE implementation often failed to read the hardware calibration state 2. When `mag_cal_state` stayed at 0, an **arc proxy fallback** kicked in that simply measured how much the user rotated their wrist (accumulating degrees of total rotation) 3. This proxy filled a progress bar to advance through states 0→1→2→3, but **didn't actually calibrate the magnetometer** 4. The UI showed "Ask an adult to help!" after a 10-second stall timer, which was confusing for the target audience **Fix applied:** Disabled the entire Pre-Flight state machine — see [Section 10](#10-changes-already-applied-pre-release). ### 5.2 — Software Calibration (gesture.py) Is Sound The gesture interpreter's own calibration is well-designed: - **Initial calibration**: Collects ~100 samples (~1 sec at rest), uses **median** (not mean) to be robust against tremor spikes - **Adaptive baseline**: Continuously drags the neutral point toward the current resting gravity vector at a slow rate (`adapt_rate = 0.002`), accommodating fatigue and posture shifts - **Motion gating**: Only adapts when `gyro_mag < 45.0 °/s` — prevents adaptation during active gestures - **Functional calibration (PCA)**: Optional axis-alignment via principal component analysis, compensating for sensor being mounted at an angle on the wrist ### 5.3 — Madgwick AHRS Filter Is Correct but Under-used The software Madgwick filter in `fusion_processor.py` is a clean implementation of 6-DOF AHRS: - Quaternion state, gradient descent correction against gravity vector - Proper dt clamping, quaternion normalization, gimbal-lock-aware Euler extraction - Linear acceleration (gravity-removed) computed correctly However, when hardware sensor fusion is active (IMUPlus mode), the Madgwick filter runs in `gesture.py` **in parallel** but its output (`euler_roll`, `euler_pitch`, `euler_yaw`) is only displayed in the calibration game's data panel. The actual game controls use the simpler low-pass gravity extraction. This is not a bug — the gravity extraction is more responsive for gaming — but it means the Madgwick filter exists as dead computation when SF is active. --- ## 6. Gesture Detection Pipeline Review ### 6.1 — Paddle Control (Tilt → velocity) Working correctly. The pipeline is: 1. Low-pass filter raw accelerometer → extract gravity vector 2. Subtract calibrated neutral → raw tilt 3. Apply functional alignment rotation (PCA yaw offset) 4. Dead-zone threshold → magnitude mapping → `paddle_velocity` [-1, 1] ### 6.2 — Flick Detection (Launch) Sound implementation using a rolling window of `gy` samples. Peak detection with cooldown prevents double-fire. Threshold is configurable per-mode (200°/s standard, 120°/s accessible). ### 6.3 — Slice Detection (`SliceDetector`) 8-frame rolling window of gyro magnitude, fires a `SliceEvent` when peak > 150°/s with 250ms cooldown. Direction classification from mean gyro components (gz = horizontal, gy = vertical). Combo counter within 1.5s sliding window. Clean, well-tested design. ### 6.4 — `get_state()` Is Fragile `GestureInterpreter.get_state()` manually copies **35 named fields** one-by-one into a new `GestureState`. Adding a new field to the dataclass without updating `get_state()` creates a silent bug where the new field is always its default value. --- ## 7. core modules untested | Add tests for sensor, gesture, fusion | | L6 | `_DE = 0.375` (dotted eighth) defined but never used in audio.py | Remove dead code | --- ## 8. Consolidated Implementation Plan ### Phase 1 — Sensor & Calibration Stabilization ✅ (Done) > [!NOTE] > These changes have already been applied. See [Section 10](#10-changes-already-applied-pre-release). - [x] Switch sensor fusion to **IMUPlus mode** (acc+gyro only, no magnetometer) - [x] Disable the broken "Pre-Flight Systems Check" in calibration game --- ### Phase 2 — Sensor Reliability (High Priority) #### 2a. Fix double `_emit_sample()` in raw fallback mode **File:** [sensor.py](file:///Users/jerold/dev/Bricks/shared/sensor.py) Add dirty flags so a sample is only emitted when both acc and gyro have been updated: ```python # Add to __init__: self._acc_dirty = False self._gyro_dirty = False # In _parse_acc: self._acc_dirty = True if self._gyro_dirty: self._emit_sample() self._acc_dirty = self._gyro_dirty = False # In _parse_gyro: self._gyro_dirty = True if self._acc_dirty: self._emit_sample() self._acc_dirty = self._gyro_dirty = False ``` #### 2b. Replace `print()` with `logging` **Files:** [sensor.py](file:///Users/jerold/dev/Bricks/shared/sensor.py), [gesture.py](file:///Users/jerold/dev/Bricks/shared/gesture.py) - Replace `print("[sensor] ...")` calls with `logger.debug()` - Keep `logger.info()` for connection/disconnection events - Add `--verbose` CLI flag to `main.py` that sets `logging.DEBUG` #### 2c. BLE disconnect detection & recovery **Files:** [gesture.py](file:///Users/jerold/dev/Bricks/shared/gesture.py), [sensor.py](file:///Users/jerold/dev/Bricks/shared/sensor.py) - In `gesture.py` `_loop()`: track consecutive `queue.Empty` timeouts. After 3 seconds of no data, set `state.sensor_disconnected = True` - In each game's draw loop: check `gs.sensor_disconnected` and render a "Sensor disconnected — press K for keyboard" overlay - In `sensor.py`: add `async def reconnect()` that re-scans and re-connects --- ### Phase 3 — Calibration Game Redesign (Medium Priority) **File:** [calibration/game.py](file:///Users/jerold/dev/Bricks/games/calibration/game.py) The Pre-Flight overlay has been disabled (Phase 1), but the calibration game should be redesigned to be genuinely useful: - **Remove dead code**: Delete `_draw_pre_flight_overlay()`, `_draw_signal_gauge()`, `_draw_takeoff_animation()`, and all `_pf_*` state variables now that Pre-Flight is permanently disabled - **Add live calibration feedback**: Show the gravity vector baseline in the roll/pitch panels. When the user holds still, show "Calibrating…" with a progress bar that reflects `gesture.py`'s actual calibration buffer fill - **Show sensor connection status**: Replace the Pre-Flight area with a simple status line: "IMUPlus | 98 Hz | Connected" or "RAW ACC/GYRO | 100 Hz | Fallback mode" - **Make the data panel more readable**: The current panel crams 30+ rows into a quarter of the screen. Group into collapsible sections or use tabs --- ### Phase 4 — Architecture Cleanup (Medium Priority) #### 4a. Extract `BaseGame` class **New file:** `shared/base_game.py` Move duplicated boilerplate from all 5 game files: - `__init__()` signature: `(screen, clock, debug, mode, audio, username, game_submode)` - `_init_layout(screen)` — scale factor, fonts, fullscreen detection - `_toggle_fullscreen()` — set mode, re-init layout - `_switch_submode()` — learn/test/play switching + learner init - `_init_learner()` — lazy GestureLearningSystem creation - Keyboard event handling: ESC→home, D→debug, F→fullscreen, L/T/G/V→learn/test - `run(gesture_src)` — main loop skeleton calling abstract `_tick(dt, gs)` and `_draw()` #### 4b. Game registry in main.py **File:** [main.py](file:///Users/jerold/dev/Bricks/main.py) Replace 5 copy-pasted game launch blocks with: ```python GAME_REGISTRY = { "bricks": BricksGame, "snake": SnakeGame, "fruit_ninja": FruitNinjaGame, "calibration": CalibrationGame, "magic_wand": MagicWandGame, } game_cls = GAME_REGISTRY[selected] game = game_cls(cur, clock, debug=debug, mode=mode, audio=audio, username=username) result = game.run(gesture_src) debug = game._debug ``` #### 4c. Fix `get_state()` fragile copy **File:** [gesture.py](file:///Users/jerold/dev/Bricks/shared/gesture.py) Replace the 35-field manual copy with: ```python def get_state(self) -> GestureState: with self._lock: return replace(self.state) ``` (`replace` is already imported from `dataclasses`) #### 4d. Replace `sys.exit(0)` with return sentinels **Files:** [home.py](file:///Users/jerold/dev/Bricks/home.py), [magic_wand/game.py](file:///Users/jerold/dev/Bricks/games/magic_wand/game.py), all games - Replace `pygame.quit(); sys.exit(0)` with `return "quit"` - In `main.py`, check for `"quit"` return and break out of the session loop --- ### Phase 5 — Polish & Testing (Lower Priority) | Item | File(s) | Change | |------|---------|--------| | Constants file | New `shared/constants.py` | `BASE_W, BASE_H = 800, 600` imported everywhere | | Font caching | `games/bricks/game.py` | Cache `PowerUp` font at init, not in `draw()` | | Calibration buffer cap | `shared/gesture.py` | `self._cal_buf = deque(maxlen=2 * cfg.calibration_samples)` | | Magic numbers → config | `shared/gesture.py` | Move `45.0`, `0.002`, `2.5 * 100`, `200.0` to `GestureConfig` | | GameResult enum | New | `class GameResult(str, Enum): HOME = "home"; QUIT = "quit"` | | Unit tests | `tests/` | `test_sensor.py` (parse_acc, parse_gyro, emit), `test_gesture.py` (calibration, tilt, flick), `test_fusion.py` (Madgwick identity, known rotation) | | Score persistence | `shared/scores.py` | JSON `data/scores/{username}.json` | | Orphaned files | `rc_car_bridge.py`, `rc_simulator.py` | Move to `examples/` | --- ### Phase 6 — Long-Term: Official SDK Migration (Future) > [!TIP] > The raw `bleak` implementation works but is a maintenance burden. Long-term, replace `shared/sensor.py` with the official MbientLab `metawear` Python SDK. This gives: > - Automatic sensor variant handling (BMI160/BMI270/BMM150) > - Built-in reconnection and data scaling > - Proper calibration data persistence to NVM > - Simplified codebase (~400 lines instead of ~900) > > The tradeoff: `libmetawear` is a native C library that must be compiled per-platform, adding a build dependency. --- ## 10. Changes Already Applied (Pre-Release) These changes were applied to the working tree before this document was finalized. ### 10a. Sensor Fusion → IMUPlus Mode **File:** [sensor.py](file:///Users/jerold/dev/Bricks/shared/sensor.py) (line 150) ```diff -_CMD_SF_MODE = bytes([_MODULE_SENSOR_FUSION, 0x02, 0x01, 0x31]) # NDOF +_CMD_SF_MODE = bytes([_MODULE_SENSOR_FUSION, 0x02, 0x02, 0x31]) # IMUPlus ``` **Effect:** Pitch and roll are now stable using only gravity as the absolute reference. The magnetometer is not used, eliminating indoor magnetic interference. ### 10b. Pre-Flight Systems Check Disabled **File:** [calibration/game.py](file:///Users/jerold/dev/Bricks/games/calibration/game.py) - All `_pf_*` state variables initialized to their "completed" values (`_pf_state=3`, `_pf_complete=True`, `_pf_takeoff_t=5.0`) - `_update_pre_flight()` replaced with a no-op pass - The draw conditionals now skip the Pre-Flight overlay since `_pf_complete=True` **Effect:** Calibration game immediately shows the 4-panel data view without the confusing progress bar sequence. ### Validation Both modified files compile without syntax errors: ``` python3 -m py_compile shared/sensor.py games/calibration/game.py # ✓ ```
